body:
[A10] **Lane 697c: milan-fpga takes its stack cores from tsn-c-stack.** Executor [A583], reviewers [R584] (internal) and [R585] (external). Branch `697-consume` from dev `8b61b709`.

**State.** The ADP, ACMP and MAAP cores, `wire.h` and their core-only tests now live in [kebag-logic/tsn-c-stack](https://github.com/kebag-logic/tsn-c-stack) (MIT, public), imported by its PR #16 with history. milan-fpga still builds its own copies under `sw/firmware/ctrl/`. Acceptance items 1-5 of this issue apply. "The chosen location" is the tsn-c-stack submodule.

**Scope.**
1. **Submodule.** Add tsn-c-stack as a submodule at `third_party/tsn-c-stack`.
   - Pin it at the newest tsn-c-stack commit whose core sources are byte-identical to milan-fpga's current copies. Find it by diffing, never by guessing.
   - The likely candidates are around `1a9f651c`, before the ADP behaviour change of tsn-c-stack PR #19 (`51870377`). Resolve the full SHA with `git rev-parse`.
   - Bumping to tsn-c-stack main, which brings that ADP change and the YAML generator (#703), is a later, separate PR.
2. **Remove the copies.** `git rm` milan-fpga's core and core-test copies. The adapters, app, loop, HAL, mailbox driver and image build compile against the submodule's headers and sources, unchanged otherwise.
   - **Both linked RV32 images (all shapes) must be byte-identical before and after.** Prove it with hashes. Any byte difference is a STOP.
   - The lwSRP pin is unchanged.
3. **Boundary gate.** A gate refuses any include from the stack into mailbox, platform, register-map or image code. A planted control must be caught. If tsn-c-stack already has an equivalent gate (`scripts/check_boundary.py`), run it from milan-fpga's gates, and add the milan-fpga-side direction.
4. **Every reference** to the old locations is updated: the builder, CI workflows, coverage ratchet, mutation tables, evidence readers, source-list gates and docs.
   - Coverage stays at 100 % with the same denominator.
   - Every mutation campaign keeps its kill counts.
   - The hosted docs gates run without submodules, and hosted runners have no RV32 compiler. Every hosted job that now needs the stack must check out the submodule, and nothing may silently skip.
5. **README.** Add a short `third_party/tsn-c-stack` note in the firmware docs: what the submodule provides, what it must not depend on, how to run its tests, and its licence (MIT inside this CERN-OHL-W platform).

STOP on any image byte difference, any change to firmware behaviour, or any lost coverage or kill. Post TAKEN, then REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.

[A10] **Pin confirmed: `1a9f651c`.** This answers the question in [A583's REVIEW READY](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/697#issuecomment-6092168627).

"Byte-identical core sources" was my wording, and it was wider than the property that matters. tsn-c-stack adds an MIT SPDX line to every file and trims comments, by design, so no commit can satisfy it. The property is that milan-fpga's firmware does not change, and two things show it:
- the cores are token-identical code at `1a9f651c`;
- every linked RV32 image is byte-identical at every shape.

Both hold. `1a9f651c` is the newest such commit, since `51870377` (tsn-c-stack #3) changes `src/adp.c`. Reviewers judge the pin against this ruling. The bump to tsn-c-stack main is the later, separate PR.

[A10] Ruling on the round-8 budget item, from hosted at `4cab445a`:
- `firmware-boundary`: 13 min 34 s of 30 (45 %).
- `firmware-verilator`: 10 min 31 s of 40 (26 %).
- `firmware-unit`: 34 min 41 s of 45 (77 %).

`firmware-unit` now runs dev's own nine steps without the capture. Its remaining runtime is dev's (26 to 37 min across recent dev runs), so its headroom is #716's scope, not this lane's. The lane's obligation was to stop adding to it, and that is met. The 60 % target is met by the two jobs this lane owns. Delta reviews R584-7 and R585-7 start at this head.

[A10] **Round 12: merge dev, scope ruling, inherited environment.** R584-10 ([6114394332](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/705#issuecomment-6114394332)) is NEGATIVE at `aca5e8af` and asks for a maintainer ruling on the hook's stated limit. The external round R585-10 ended early on a provider error and is void. Its local report described a crafted environment key that the hook accepted; item 3 below covers that case. PR #705 also conflicts with dev `09c7231e`: F-INT (PR #704) changed `.github/workflows/rtl-fast.yml` and `scripts/ci_events.py`. Executor [A583].

1. **Merge dev `09c7231e`** with a merge commit. Keep F-INT's firmware steps and this lane's `firmware-boundary` and `firmware-verilator` jobs. Then `ci_events.py --check` and `--selftest`, `act_ci.py --selftest` and the affected firmware suites must pass. PR #724 (#716) splits `firmware-unit` and touches the same files; whichever of the two merges second resolves.

2. **Scope ruling (R584-10 option a).**
   - The pin proof's threat model is the state it reads: the checkout's files and modes, Git's object store, refs, configuration and attributes, and the environment the proof inherits.
   - Code inside the proof's own modules is reviewed source and is outside that model. A rebinding of `sys.audit`, or a crafted object built inside those modules, is a source change that review sees.
   - The runtime hook stays as defence in depth.
   - The README, the docstring and the PR body state this model in place of "native code is the remaining limit".
   - From this round on, a finding that needs adversarial code inside the proof's own modules is out of scope: at most a SUGGESTION, never a reason to withhold POSITIVE.

3. **In scope and required: the inherited environment.**
   - The helper builds Git's environment from an explicit allowlist instead of inheriting it, so no inherited variable can redirect the repository, object store, configuration or replace base. That covers `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, `GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE`, `GIT_CONFIG_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`SYSTEM` and `GIT_ATTR_*`.
   - Keys and values are plain `str`, and the hook judges exactly the mapping that is passed.
   - Standing controls set each of those variables in the caller's environment. Each must be neutralised or refused by name, and the clean proof must still pass.
   - Add a control for a configuration-injected clean filter (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`KEY`/`VALUE`).

STOP if the dev merge cannot keep both sides' CI guarantees, or if any image changes a byte.

Post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.

[A10] **Round 13: the way on from the round-12 STOP.** tsn-c-stack #21 is complete. Its PR #22 head `405dc683` is the round-12 pin `1a9f651c` plus F-INT's ACMP publish port and its tests. Its ACMP core is token-identical to milan-fpga dev's copies, with code-line positions kept, and all six same-flag RV32 object pairs are byte-equal. tsn-c-stack allows squash merges only, so `405dc683` is kept reachable by the tag `milan-fpga-697-pin-405dc683`, and main `1ba27354` carries the same content through #23. Executor [A583].

1. **Move the pin** of `third_party/tsn-c-stack` to `405dc683`, the tagged commit, not main: main also carries #19 and #20, which would change the firmware. Re-record everything the pin feeds through its generators: the pin proof's records, the submodule docs and diagram, and the boundary.
2. **Merge current dev** with a merge commit. On the ACMP core files, keep the deletions: the core now comes from the submodule, which has the port. Keep dev's adapter (`acmp_mbx.*`) and its `publish` wiring. Resolve the CI files so that F-INT's firmware steps and this lane's `firmware-boundary` and `firmware-verilator` jobs both run. PR #724 (#716) touches the same CI files; whichever merges second resolves.
3. **Retarget F-INT's 11 `pub-acmp-*` plants** in `ctrl_mutants.py` to `third_party/tsn-c-stack/src/acmp.c`, so each still fails by name.
4. The firmware images must be byte-identical to dev's images at the merged dev for every shape. Prove it.
5. Keep round 12's threat-model texts and environment allowlist, and all 79 pin controls.

STOP if any image differs, or if any F-INT plant cannot be retargeted.

Post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.

[A10] **Round 19: merge dev `d5858bbe` (M8a, PR #721).** PR #705 holds two POSITIVE reviews at `27ee16b5` (R584-16 and R585-17). M8a merged as dev `d5858bbe`, and it conflicts with this branch in one file, `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/ctrl_srp_image.py`. Executor [A583].

1. **Merge dev `d5858bbe`** with a merge commit, no rebase. Resolve `ctrl_srp_image.py` so that both sides stand: M8a's on-chip split control memory and firmware-owned reset entry, and this branch's stack cores from the tsn-c-stack submodule and its pin checks. No check is dropped or doubled.
2. **No other change.** The images at the head equal dev `d5858bbe`'s, entry for entry, for every shape. All pin controls still hold. STOP if the merge needs any change to firmware behaviour, an image input or the pin.
3. **Re-run round 18's bar** at the merge head. Record the resolution in HANDOFF.md and the PR body. Apply R584-16-RES-1 and RES-2 to the body.

Post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.

[A10] **Ruling on the [round 19 STOP](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/697#issuecomment-6135151826): extend the scope to classify M8a's three programs.** The merge `95ca54cb` is correct: 65 of 65 images equal dev `d5858bbe`, and the pin is unchanged. The refusal is the boundary gate doing its job on new programs from dev. Executor [A583].

1. **Classify each program on evidence of what it runs, not its name:**
   - `sw/litex/test_ctrl_memory.py` compiles the firmware reset entry (`:540`). It is a firmware builder. Its compiler invocations are captured by the capture shim, like the four builders, and judged by the boundary. Add it as a fifth capture in the gate, and in the `firmware-boundary` job if that job runs the captures, within that job's 60 % headroom.
   - `sw/litex/ctrl_memory.py` and `sw/litex/milan_soc.py`: if they launch no compiler and build no firmware, classify them `OUTSIDE`, each with a one-line reason. If either does compile firmware, treat it like `test_ctrl_memory.py`.
2. **Controls.** For each, add a planted control showing the classification is load-bearing: an unclassified copy is refused, and a planted out-of-boundary include in the reset-entry compile is caught through the fifth capture.
3. **Finish round 18's bar** at the new head, which the STOP left incomplete: coverage, the firmware execution and mutation campaigns, both boundary sides, and the remaining entry-point, hook and configuration campaigns. The images still equal dev `d5858bbe`, and the pin is unchanged.

STOP only if the reset-entry compile reads a source the boundary must refuse, which would be a real coupling to report. Post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.

[A583] REVIEW READY — Round 19 continuation

Head: `97e713168470bfae2685521fa557dc462b782b32` (local only; not pushed).
Base merge retained: `95ca54cb`, with dev `d5858bbee328cf8d2c39a99ec14203f5d0ddd123` as its second parent.

The scope extension in comment 6137497435 is implemented. `test_ctrl_memory.py --build-only` is a fifth mandatory compiler capture; the unchanged probe/link helper is shared with the full suite. Each of the three programs has a load-bearing unclassified-copy control. Dropping the fifth capture refuses it by name, and a private stack-header include in the reset entry is caught through that capture. The baseline reset compile reads no forbidden source.

Classification scope is explicit: `ctrl_memory.py` compiles nothing. `milan_soc.py` is OUTSIDE relative to this control firmware: it loads a prelinked control ELF; its separate BIOS/milan_baremetal path builds other firmware and compiles no control-stack source. The reason does not claim that the entire program compiles nothing.

Local evidence, final required commands all rc 0:
- 65/65 linked ELFs equal dev by direct bytes, size and SHA-256; both manifests hash to `96f55deba3b69b224fb838b746f559b3c944b552c694cef3211470d8b11db584`. The tsn-c-stack pin remains `405dc68310a18f669049ffc10cc23eef7300dcff`; no production firmware or image input changed in the continuation.
- Firmware boundary: 2824 sources / 3052 invocations; 110 boundary, 106 pin and four figure controls, no findings or misbehavior. Verilator boundary: 829 / 926; six boundary, 106 pin and four figure controls, no findings or misbehavior.
- All 915 firmware verdicts pass: 60 arms, 506 control, 76 AECP, 198/73 SRP and two lwSRP pin controls. Store execution: 435 tests across five shapes. Memory suite: 44/44 mutants caught.
- Coverage: 30 files at 100% lines/branches after unchanged exclusions; candidate and dev tables match under the same compiler; 29/29 reader controls pass.
- Entry points: 252/252 named refusals. Pin matrix, hook rule-removal, configuration variants and the earlier unchanged review probes retain their expected outcomes on both Git versions and both Python versions.
- CI contract: 2169 checks and 3064 self-test arms; 16 additional workflow plants caught. All 54 documentation/source-list/evidence commands pass. Disposable runner self-test: 446 arms pass.
- Boundary phases plus measured dependency installation total 836.57 s locally, 46.5% of the unchanged 30-minute timeout. This is a sum of bounded foreground commands, not new hosted timing. The four prior firmware jobs and their hosted budget evidence remain unchanged.

The handoff and prepared PR body contain the changed file:line table, full image/coverage/mutation tables, pin diff/proof, commands, receipts and limitations. R584-16-RES-1/RES-2 and the corresponding R585-17 residue remain applied. The newer native environment changes one mutant's failed-check count from 32 to 35, while its caught verdict is unchanged; the coverage comparison with dev is exact under that environment.

Supplementary store `--self-test` attempts reached the 570-second command limit and are not counted as passes; no complete 109-mutant store claim is made. Round 18's required store command omits that option and passes all 435 tests. The separate BIOS classification scope is stated above for review.

The tree and both submodule checkouts are clean. This head needs independent review and protected hosted contexts after publication; prior positive reviews cover `27ee16b5`. No push, PR edit, merge or hardware operation was performed.
